## Summary

This page lists every current leaf value in chart defaults, checked-in overlays, GitOps values and manifests, release values, and infrastructure manifests. Open a file section to inspect its nested fields. The inventory redacts credentials, identities, and access lists. A redacted value remains configurable, but this page never publishes its content.

## Recursive Value Reference

Each leaf row separates the checked-in source from the runtime receiver. It follows local Helm templates, Argo CD value-file bindings, and Kubernetes resource authorities. An external chart or Kubernetes API owns validation when its schema is outside this repository. A field with no active deployment binding is identified as inactive instead of being presented as an effective option.

charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml:339 | Changes whether startup prepares credentials and a chart-managed repository checkout; `runAsRoot` also changes the SSH path, modes, and ownership.<br>Failure: This chart has no Boolean schema for this field. Helm treats every non-empty string, including the string `"false"`, as true in its condition receiver. Use the YAML Boolean values `true` and `false`; do not quote them. With `true`, a missing SSH Secret, invalid repository URL, authentication failure, or dirty or incompatible checkout can stop initialization. With `false`, repository-dependent work has no chart-managed checkout. |

Helm treats every non-empty string, including the string `"false"`, as true in its condition receiver. Its raw scalar receiver is parsed again as YAML or JSON, so the receiving format or API decides whether another type is accepted. Use the YAML Boolean values `true` and `false`; do not quote them. A missing Secret or key, or malformed generated JSON, prevents startup. With Boolean `false`, Discord command ingress is disabled. A quoted `"false"` splits receiver behavior: Helm branches enable bindings and token wiring, while unquoted JSON interpolation still emits the JSON Boolean `false`. |

| `$.agent.git.enabled` | Controls chart-managed SSH setup and Git synchronization into `/workspace/git-repo`. ## Deployed Configuration Payloads

The chart embeds each file below in the swarm ConfigMap and the init process materializes it in runtime configuration. YAML and JSON files are expanded to every leaf. Executable JavaScript and HCL files remain complete, digest-pinned files because treating their syntax as ordinary key/value data would invent semantics. A payload without a checked-in reader is identified as tool- or image-owned.

- [`charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml:1226`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/2b95ae38389dae19ccf26778051fc191852774b3/charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml#L1226-L1226) — init container mounts the ConfigMap at /init-swarm-config.
- [`charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml:665`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/2b95ae38389dae19ccf26778051fc191852774b3/charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml#L665-L665) — lint-policy.json is copied from the ConfigMap mount into persistent /config.
- [`charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml:695`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/2b95ae38389dae19ccf26778051fc191852774b3/charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml#L695-L695) — lint-policy.json is copied or rendered from /config into /runtime-config.

Source selection and retention:

When the mounted chart file exists, it replaces the persistent file. When it is absent, the existing persistent file remains. The runtime copy uses the resulting persistent file.

- [`charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml:664`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/2b95ae38389dae19ccf26778051fc191852774b3/charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml#L664-L664) — the chart source replaces persistent lint-policy.json only when the mounted source file exists.

Runtime reader boundary:

The repository proves a parser for request.policyPath, but it does not bind that request field to /runtime-config/lint-policy.json. Materialization and parsing are separate proved boundaries, not a continuous runtime chain.

Related evidence that does not close the boundary:

- [`skills/nova/plugins/lint/src/engine/index.ts:84`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/2b95ae38389dae19ccf26778051fc191852774b3/skills/nova/plugins/lint/src/engine/index.ts#L84-L84) — the lint request chooses a path, but checked-in source does not bind it to the chart runtime copy.
- [`skills/nova/plugins/lint/src/engine/policy.ts:262`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/2b95ae38389dae19ccf26778051fc191852774b3/skills/nova/plugins/lint/src/engine/policy.ts#L262-L262) — the lint engine parses whichever request-selected path it receives.

## Runtime Meaning

| Value group | Runtime effect | Expected proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| image and pull secrets | selects agent and sidecar images, tags, pull policy, and GHCR pull Secret | rendered Deployments include expected image refs and `imagePullSecrets` |
| auth/provider/Discord/Stitch/LiteLLM | selects direct values or existing Secret name/key references | rendered env refs point to expected Secret keys and generated secrets reference lists those keys |
| persistence | creates workspace/config PVCs for gateway and plugin-runtime state | rendered PVCs and security contexts match production values |
| service and extra ports | exposes gateway/bridge ClusterIP ports plus explicit extra NodePorts | rendered Services contain only documented ports |
| buster namespace broker | adds lease CRD/RBAC/controller and controller env vars | Buster render includes CRD, lease client RBAC, controller Deployment, and namespace fence docs |
| probes, startup doctor, and dependency checks | configures gateway, Redis, and LiteLLM health checks; `gateway.startupDoctor` runs `openclaw doctor --fix` as a blocking state update while the gateway is stopped | rendered init container, env vars, and smoke commands exercise the health and doctor surfaces |

## Failure Signals

- A top-level value appears in this page but has no rendered effect: add deployment truth coverage or remove the stale value.
- Rendered Secret refs do not match `my-values/setup-secrets.sh`: update values, helper, inventory, and docs together.
- Buster values disable sandbox/broker behavior unexpectedly: inspect `my-values/buster-values.yaml` before changing chart templates.
- A live pod keeps old config after values change: remember the init container preserves persisted config unless override flags request replacement.
